algorithm.Title: Heart Rate and Heartbeat Questions - Female (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Female
Definition: UAT-only assessment of a fast, pounding, fluttering, slow, or irregular heartbeat across adult and pediatric patients; not approved for real-patient or production use.

Background.ExpertReviewer: Pending qualified Qatar adult, pediatric, obstetric, cardiac, and pharmacy review

FirstAid: Call Qatar 999 now. Do not drive or allow the patient to drive. Keep them at rest and follow dispatcher instructions; do not give food, drink, or an extra dose of heart medicine unless directed by an emergency clinician. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Was a faint or temporary loss of consciousness the main event?
questions.Information: A faint or temporary loss of consciousness belongs in the Fainting pathway.

questions.Question: Are palpitations present now with chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, fainting or near-fainting, seizure, blue/grey color, severe weakness, confusion, or inability to wake normally?
questions.Information: NHS.UK heart palpitations guidance lists these as emergency-assessment criteria. Do not drive yourself to the emergency department.

questions.Question: Do palpitations keep recurring, last several minutes or longer, or occur in a child, during pregnancy or postpartum, with fever/dehydration/bleeding, known heart disease, family history of sudden cardiac death, stimulant exposure, or a new or changed medicine?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends seeing a doctor for recurring or persistent palpitations, especially with cardiac risk factors.

questions.Question: For an otherwise well adult who is not pregnant or recently postpartum, is this a brief, occasional episode with a clear benign trigger and none of the emergency, urgent, medicine, or cardiac-risk features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes palpitations from lifestyle triggers as often not needing treatment.

advice.Title: Emergency palpitations precautions
Content: Call Qatar 999 now. Do not drive or allow the patient to drive. Keep them at rest and follow dispatcher instructions; do not give food, drink, or an extra dose of heart medicine unless directed by an emergency clinician. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: worsening chest pain or breathing; loss of consciousness, seizure, or blue/grey color.

advice.Title: Urgent palpitations review
Content: Arrange prompt in-person assessment through the Qatar pathway approved for this UAT environment; an ECG and review of medicines and contributing illness may be required. Do not advise starting, stopping, or taking an extra dose of a cardiac, thyroid, stimulant, or other medicine by telephone.
Call Back If: episodes become more frequent, longer, or continuous; chest pain, breathing difficulty, faintness, or altered responsiveness develops.

advice.Title: Managing lifestyle-related palpitations
Content: Avoid known triggers such as stress, caffeine, alcohol, smoking, recreational drugs, strenuous exercise, and sleep deprivation.
Call Back If: palpitations become more frequent or last longer; chest pain or fainting develops.
